name: Podcasts
blurb:
This section curates podcasts covering AI research, engineering, and industry strategy, tracking each show's host, focus, and whether transcripts are published, rather than pulling from a live episode feed or download-ranking data.

Each entry is manually reviewed and its listing is checked against the show's own site, most recently on September 5, 2026, for every podcast currently listed. That means the section reflects editorial judgment about which shows are worth a reader's time, not an algorithmic popularity ranking, and it will not automatically surface new or emerging shows the way a review-count-based directory might.

As of this verification pass, six shows are listed. The Cognitive Revolution, hosted by Nathan Labenz, and the Dwarkesh Podcast, hosted by Dwarkesh Patel, are positioned as capability and strategy analysis with published transcripts. Latent Space, from swyx and Alessio Fanelli, is described as the AI engineering podcast of record, also with transcripts. Practical AI, with Chris Benson and Daniel Whitenack, and The TWIML AI Podcast, hosted by Sam Charrington, round out the applied and long-running interview side, both with transcripts or detailed show notes. The Lex Fridman Podcast is included for its long-form AI researcher interviews but only has selected transcripts published, rather than a full archive like the others. Episode cadence varies widely by show, from weekly interview formats to more sporadic long-form releases, and this section does not track episode count, release schedule, or download rankings for any of the shows it lists.

reading.body:
These six podcasts collectively document AI capability development through interviews with researchers and builders, with most publishing full transcripts for searchability and reference.

The shows span two distinct audiences. Three focus on technical depth: Latent Space interviews engineers building systems, Practical AI targets working practitioners, and The TWIML AI Podcast archives a decade of applied machine learning. Three prioritize strategic conversation: The Cognitive Revolution analyzes capability and strategy, Dwarkesh Podcast conducts research-depth interviews with lab leaders, and Lex Fridman's AI episodes capture canonical researcher discussions. This division reflects how AI knowledge now moves through specialized channels rather than unified venues.

Transcript publication matters for the infrastructure of knowledge in a field moving faster than written analysis can track. Full transcripts make these conversations searchable, quotable, and citable in ways audio alone cannot support. For understanding how AI scaling relates to compute and infrastructure, the strategic interviews documenting lab leaders' reasoning are more valuable than the applied-engineering shows, though both preserve reasoning that would otherwise remain private.

This collection does not cover why these particular hosts and shows achieved prominence, does not measure audience size, and does not include podcasts focused on AI policy, ethics, or business strategy outside technical capability. It captures what speakers choose to say in long-form conversations, not what researchers write when making formal claims.
